functions.get_item(sku): returns dict {sku: str, name: str, price: float dollars (12.5 = $12.50), category: str}, or None if sku unknown
functions.get_customer(customer_id): returns dict {id: str, name: str, discount: float fraction (0.10 = 10%), region: str code as in data e.g. TX}, or None if id unknown
functions.discounted_price(sku, customer_id): returns float dollars = price * (1 - discount), unrounded; None if sku or customer unknown

value.notes: Only pricing.py reads data_pricing/. Unknown keys return None, never raise. No tax is computed in pricing.py; tax.py takes region from get_customer().

why: Agreed shape for pricing lookups: dict results, dollars as float, discounts as fractions, None for unknown keys, so invoice.py and tax.py can call it directly.

value: tax.compute_tax(lines, region, discount_pct=0) -> int. lines: list of (category: str, amount_cents: int) for ALL line items of the order (taxable and exempt). region: str region code of the customer (e.g. "TX"), or None for an unknown customer -> returns 0. discount_pct: customer discount in percent numbers (e.g. 10 = 10%), default 0; must be 0..100 else ValueError. Returns total tax for the order as an integer number of cents. Category matching is exact and case-sensitive against the strings in data_tax/exempt_categories.csv. Rounding: computed exactly (no floats), rounded half up to the cent once, at the end. Also provided: tax.tax_rate(region) -> percent number (8.25 etc.; None -> 0), tax.is_exempt(category) -> bool. Raises KeyError for a non-None region not in data_tax/rates.csv.
why: Lines are (category, cents) so tax.py alone applies exemptions; discount is applied to the taxable sum only, as RULES.md says; integers in cents / percent numbers per team standard. Customer-level info (region, discount) is passed in by invoice/pricing caller.

value: Unknown customer is signalled by region=None (caller passes None when the customer or its region is not known) -> tax 0. A region string that is not in rates.csv raises KeyError (team standard: lookup that finds nothing raises KeyError). This reconciles RULES.md (unknown customer pays 0%) with the team KeyError rule.
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, but the team standard says a failed lookup raises KeyError. Making the unknown case an explicit None argument satisfies both without silently taxing 0 on a typo like "Tx".

Matches invoice.py: I pass region=None when get_customer returns None, and show the customer id.
